heroPool.FACT_EXPLANATION: Naked dragonfish possess specialized infrared-sensitive cells on their retinas that allow them to detect the tiny heat emitted by smaller fish and crustaceans. Juvenile deep-sea researchers observed that these fish often orient their attacks solely based on thermal cues in near-total darkness. Their elongated bodies and fang-like teeth complement infrared hunting by enabling rapid, precise strikes. Infrared detection improves hunting efficiency in an environment where bioluminescence is often sparse or absent. The thermal system works alongside lateral line mechanoreceptors to detect prey movement and orientation. Observations indicate that dragonfish can detect differences as subtle as 0.005°C. Evolution has refined this capability over millions of years to maintain energy efficiency in extreme food-scarce habitats. Infrared perception also aids predator avoidance, sensing larger predators before visual detection is possible. This adaptation demonstrates that deep-sea giants rely on hidden senses beyond mere eyesight.
heroPool.DID_YOU_KNOW: Naked dragonfish can detect the faint body heat of prey several meters away, even when no light is present in the abyss.

heroPool.SEO_TITLE: The Mayan Death Masks: Faces That Outlived Bodies
heroPool.FACT_HOOK: Some Mayans literally wore their ancestors’ faces to eternity.
heroPool.FACT_EXPLANATION: The Classic Maya (250–900 CE) practiced a ritual of creating death masks from jade, obsidian, or plaster, modeled over the deceased’s face. These masks were often painted or gilded, preserving facial features for the afterlife. Wealthy individuals, including rulers, were adorned with these masks inside tombs or pyramids, serving as both protection and representation. Archaeologists in Guatemala have uncovered masks buried alongside rich offerings like cacao, textiles, and ceremonial objects. Some masks were surprisingly lifelike, capturing expressions and facial contours with precision. The Maya believed that preserving the visage allowed the soul to recognize its body in the afterlife. Funerary texts describe masks as gateways to divine favor. The practice was both artistic and spiritual, bridging mortality with immortality.
heroPool.DID_YOU_KNOW: Some Mayan death masks were made of jade mosaics glued over plaster molds to perfectly replicate facial features.

This sensory adaptation is particularly valuable during vertical migrations when light levels are extremely low. Infrared vision works in conjunction with lateral line detection to form a precise, multi-modal perception of the environment. Field studies indicate that lanternfish can detect temperature differences of just 0.002°C. This adaptation provides an advantage in energy conservation and predator avoidance.
